summary: In Greek mythology, Dolops (Ancient Greek: Δόλοψ) was a Trojan warrior, bravest son of Lampus son of Laomedon and skilled with the spear. In the Iliad he nearly killed Meges before Menelaus struck him from behind; the Greeks then stripped his armour.

sections.heading: Fight with Meges and Menelaus
paragraphs: When Meges son of Phyleus leapt upon Polydamas and missed, then set about stripping Croesmus, Dolops sprang upon him and drove his spear against Meges' shield; the cunningly wrought corslet stayed the point. As Meges fought back, Menelaus attacked Dolops from behind and killed him, whereupon the Achaeans removed his armour.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This atlas entry (dolops-trojan) is the Trojan son of Lampus. Distinct from Dolops son of Clytius, the Achaean Hector slew (dolops-clytiid), and from the other Dolopes of Cronus, Hermes, and Lemnos listed on the shared Wikipedia name-page.
